claims.assertion: The driver cancelled the trip at 09:54:25 and a $6.61 cancellation fee was charged to the rider; under NS-0 that fee only stands if the driver's no-show claim satisfies NS-1 in full.

The driver's own written statement claims he waited and cancelled the rider as a no-show, but the same timeline records no "I'm Here" tap, so the statement is contradicted by the system record and cannot sustain the fee.

In the alternative, even if the timeline fact F6 ("I'm Here" tapped 09:50:45, stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap) is preferred over F7, the rider was charged $6.61 while the driver's GPS-stationary wait is recorded as only 4 min 0 s (09:50:25–09:54:25) and the rider had already told the driver at 09:52 he was two minutes away — the rider was not given the claimed 3-minute-plus window in a way that justifies the full fee.

Chat #3 at 09:54 from the driver — "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it." — contains a threat keyword detected at 09:54, and it was sent 25 seconds before the cancellation; NS-1's fee cannot stand where the cancellation followed a threat rather than an ordinary no-show.

Because the driver cancelled while asserting a no-show that is not established (no "I'm Here" record and a threat immediately preceding cancellation), the fee is not owed by the rider and the $6.61 must be refunded in full.

The rider's account has zero disputes and zero upheld disputes in 90 days (rating 4.6), so there is no pattern on the rider's side that could explain the charge, whereas the driver's account shows 3 disputes and 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days.
The rider's complaint of threatening chat language is an independent safety event and should be referred for human handling rather than decided by this fee ruling.
The fee was charged on a 1.0x-surge trip, so the full $6.61 on record is the whole disputed amount and is refundable without any surge adjustment.

weaknesses: The system record is internally inconsistent and the other side will pick the version that hurts the rider: F6 (timeline) says the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:50:45 and stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap, which on its own would satisfy NS-1(i) and (iii); I rely on F7 ("driver_pressed_here_at is null") to defeat that, and the judge may prefer F6.

F2 (gps) and F5 (timeline) both show the driver within 200 m of the pickup for 4 min 20 s and arriving at 09:50:05, which supports the driver's assertion that he waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup — the very condition NS-1(iii) requires.
F3 confirms the driver was genuinely stationary 39 m from the pickup for 4 minutes, so I cannot argue he was not present; my case turns on the "I'm Here" precondition and the threat, not on absence.

The rider's own message F11 ("2 min, coming" at 09:52) shows the rider was not at the pickup point when he said he would be; the driver will use F11 plus F3/F2 to argue an honest no-show and that at least part of the $6.61 was earned under NS-1.
F14 is the driver's statement only and loses to system records, but it is the only narrative the driver needs if the judge accepts F6 over F7.

The threat in F12 is only relevant to SAFE-1 escalation and to the equities of the cancellation; it does not by itself prove the no-show test failed, and the rider's profile (F18) is clean but profile facts cannot decide the case.

In the alternative, even if the timeline fact F6 ("I'm Here" tapped 09:50:45, stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap) is preferred over F7, the rider was charged $6.61 while the driver's GPS-stationary wait is recorded as only 4 min 0 s (09:50:25–09:54:25) and the rider had already told the driver at 09:52 he was two minutes away — the rider was not given the claimed 3-minute-plus window in a way that justifies the full fee.

Chat #3 at 09:54 from the driver — "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it." — contains a threat keyword detected at 09:54, and it was sent 25 seconds before the cancellation; NS-1's fee cannot stand where the cancellation followed a threat rather than an ordinary no-show.

Because the driver cancelled while asserting a no-show that is not established (no "I'm Here" record and a threat immediately preceding cancellation), the fee is not owed by the rider and the $6.61 must be refunded in full.

The rider's account has zero disputes and zero upheld disputes in 90 days (rating 4.6), so there is no pattern on the rider's side that could explain the charge, whereas the driver's account shows 3 disputes and 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days.
The rider's complaint of threatening chat language is an independent safety event and should be referred for human handling rather than decided by this fee ruling.
The fee was charged on a 1.0x-surge trip, so the full $6.61 on record is the whole disputed amount and is refundable without any surge adjustment.

weaknesses: The system record is internally inconsistent and the other side will pick the version that hurts the rider: F6 (timeline) says the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:50:45 and stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap, which on its own would satisfy NS-1(i) and (iii); I rely on F7 ("driver_pressed_here_at is null") to defeat that, and the judge may prefer F6.

F2 (gps) and F5 (timeline) both show the driver within 200 m of the pickup for 4 min 20 s and arriving at 09:50:05, which supports the driver's assertion that he waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup — the very condition NS-1(iii) requires.
F3 confirms the driver was genuinely stationary 39 m from the pickup for 4 minutes, so I cannot argue he was not present; my case turns on the "I'm Here" precondition and the threat, not on absence.

The rider's own message F11 ("2 min, coming" at 09:52) shows the rider was not at the pickup point when he said he would be; the driver will use F11 plus F3/F2 to argue an honest no-show and that at least part of the $6.61 was earned under NS-1.
F14 is the driver's statement only and loses to system records, but it is the only narrative the driver needs if the judge accepts F6 over F7.

The threat in F12 is only relevant to SAFE-1 escalation and to the equities of the cancellation; it does not by itself prove the no-show test failed, and the rider's profile (F18) is clean but profile facts cannot decide the case.

claims.assertion: The $6.61 cancellation fee was validly earned on the no-show branch of NS-0 (cancelled_by = driver on a rider no-show claim).
The driver was at the pick-up point according to GPS: closest approach 38 m and first inside 200 m at 09:50:05, satisfying NS-1(ii).

The driver waited well past the 3-minute threshold — 4 min 20 s cumulative within 200 m before cancellation (F2), stationary 09:50:25–09:54:25 (F3) — satisfying NS-1(iii), so the fee stands and the outcome should be no_action.
The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:50:45 and remained within 200 m for 3 min 40 s afterwards, meeting the button-tap element of NS-1(i).
The rider's own message at 09:52 confirmed she was not yet at the car ("2 min, coming"), corroborating that the rider did not show within the waiting window.
We accept the driver's 09:54 message was a threat and that it triggers escalation of the conduct issue only, without disturbing the fare finding under NS-1.
The driver's history is at most an additional-action input: 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 d of 1176 trips could support flag_account, and profile facts cannot decide this case alone.

weaknesses: F7 records driver_pressed_here_at as null, which directly contradicts the F6 timeline that the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:50:45 — the rider will argue NONE of NS-1(i) is met, and under the rule that system records beat statements, F7 (timeline) must be squared against F5/F6.

F12/F13 (threat: "I will find you and you will regret it") will be pressed hard by the rider: even if the fee survives, SAFE-1 forces escalate and the conduct can justify account action against the driver (F19's 2 upheld no-shows).
The cumulative in-range time (F2: 4 min 20 s) only just clears the 3-minute threshold, so any argument about when the clock started (acceptance 09:47 vs. arrival 09:50) is contestable on F4/F5.

points.response: Conceded as a routing matter: the cancellation was recorded as cancelled_by = driver at 09:54:25 with a $6.61 fee on record (F4, F8), so NS-0 sends the case to NS-1 — but NS-0 is only the gateway, and the fee still requires every NS-1 element to be met.

Conceded on proximity but it proves nothing by itself: F1 and F2 show the driver near the pickup, yet NS-1(ii) is only one of three cumulative conditions, and satisfying the geolocation element cannot supply the missing "I'm Here" record under F7.

The in-range clock the driver relies on is itself in dispute and does not reach the outcome he wants: F3 shows him stationary only 4 min 0 s (09:50:25–09:54:25) and F5 puts recorded arrival at 09:50:05 with cancellation 4 min 20 s later, so at most NS-1(iii) is marginal — and NS-1 requires (i), (ii) AND (iii), so a bare margin on one element cannot carry the fee.

This is the contested element and the system record beats the narrative: F7 states driver_pressed_here_at is null (the driver never tapped "I'm Here"), which directly contradicts F6, so on the record NS-1(i) fails and NS-2 mandates full refund of the $6.61.

F11 shows the rider communicating and approaching ("2 min, coming" at 09:52), not refusing to show; that is inconsistent with a bad-faith no-show and is why the driver's 09:54 threat to "find you" (F12, F13) followed instead of a further wait.

We agree the threat is an independent safety matter requiring referral (F12, F13), but the driver cannot quarantine it from the fare finding: the threat was sent at 09:54 and the cancellation followed at 09:54:25 (F4), so the cancellation was the act of a driver who had just threatened the rider, and NS-2 refunds the fee.

We accept profile facts are an additional-action input only (F19), but they are admissible here: the driver already has 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F19) while the rider has 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days (F18), and combined with the threat in F12 this supports a flag_account referral on the driver whether or not the fare finding favours him.
Restated, not withdrawn: the fee on record is $6.61 with no surge (F8, F9), and because NS-1(i) fails on F7 the whole disputed amount is refundable under NS-2.

For the record on the safety limb, the traffic and weather facts show a fair, dry trip with no incidents or congestion (F15, F16, F17), so nothing external explains either the threat or the cancellation — the conduct stands on F12/F13 alone and goes to human handling.
Conceded as a correct reading of NS-0: because cancelled_by = driver on a no-show claim, the $6.61 stands only if NS-1 is satisfied — but F5, F2 and F3 show it is.

The null field in F7 is contradicted by the timeline fact F6, which affirmatively records the "I'm Here" tap at 09:50:45 (42 m from pickup) and continued presence within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap; where the two records conflict on this element, the party bearing the fee does not get to cherry-pick the null.

F14 is not needed: the driver's case rests on system records F6, F2 and F3, which independently establish arrival, the tap and the waiting duration, so the rider's "statement loses to records" point cuts against the case the driver actually makes.

On the rider's own premise (F6 preferred), NS-1 is satisfied in full: tap at 09:50:45 plus within-200 m time of 3 min 40 s after the tap exceeds the 3:01 threshold, and F2/F3 record 4 min 20 s in range and a stationary 4 min at 39 m — the rider's F11 promise of "2 min" at 09:52 was itself unmet, which is exactly the no-show the fee covers.

The threat in F12/F13 is a conduct matter routed under SAFE-1 to human handling — it has no textual hook in NS-2, whose only trigger is the failure of NS-1(i)(ii)(iii), all three of which are met here; a bad message sent 25 s before a valid cancellation does not convert a valid no-show into a refund.
Refund_full under NS-2 requires NS-1(i), (ii) or (iii) to fail; F6, F1/F2 and F2/F3 satisfy all three respectively, so the $6.61 was earned and no_action is the correct outcome.

Profile facts cannot decide a case, and F18 is not exculpatory of the no-show itself: F11 shows the rider was still absent at 09:52, and F19's 2 upheld no-show disputes over 1176 trips in 90 d is at most an additional-action input, not proof of this ride's outcome.
Agreed that the threat language in F12/F13 goes to human handling under SAFE-1; that escalation is parallel to, and does not dissolve, the fee finding under NS-1.
Accepted that F8/F9 fix the disputed sum at $6.61 with no surge component — the only issue is whether NS-1 is met, and F6/F2/F3 show it is.

To keep my own record straight: I maintain that the fee finding survives, but I withdraw the suggestion that the threat is a mere aside — F12/F13 warrant SAFE-1 escalation, and I do not oppose account review of the driver's conduct while asking that the fare outcome remain no_action.
